difficulty_reason: After divisor/chip-firing basics and Seymour-Thomas bramble duality, the remaining task is to optimize support over all equivalent effective divisors, then synchronize the first lost and later gained bramble members along the canonical nested firing chain. The authors construct a cut hitting set using a bramble member with minimal shore intersection and force a degree bound from the separated bramble sides; this global support/cut construction is not supplied by standard reduction or duality alone. The full chain, support-side and cut-hitting-set human cores are retained, as uncounted support for one Theorem3.1.
